newsitem.title: UK: UK green rate change possible March 14 - HGCA says.
newsitem.headline: UK green rate change possible March 14 - HGCA says.

text.p: Sterling's green rate could be revalued again on March 14, the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority said.
The UK's green rate was revalued on Tuesday, when the rate changed to 0.768177 to the Ecu, from the previous 0.809915.
Sterling is due on Thursday to enter the first of what could be five 10-day confirmation periods, ending on March 13, ahead of a change the following day.

This move, along with the round of green rate devaluations which take place on Thursday, has been triggered by the so-called 'three-day' rule, which is designed to take account of sharp currency movements.
Under the rule, changes can be made if there are large moves over just three days, rather than the usual 10-day period.
When any currency is in the confirmation periods, the three-day rule is suspended, but the sterling green rate revaluation on Tuesday brought the rule back into operation.
One effect of a green rate revaluation is to cut farm incomes. UK farmers are expected to get a freeze in the green rates used to convert direct payments.

And the National Farmers' Union is campaigning for compensation payments, which have been made in other countries where there have been revaluations, to counter other income losses caused by the change.
Green rates are used by the EU to convert amounts set in Ecu under its Common Agricultural Policy into national currencies.
